title: A Man Who Keeps Moving
summary: Open on Brandon as an ordinary drifter crossing the Sunfields in Jessie's battered rig. The narrator establishes the simple truth of who he is before anyone else gets a chance to rename him.

panelPlan.text: Wide opening panel across the top: hard white Sunfields under a huge pale sky. Jessie's battered rig is a small moving shape on the road, with a half-buried black Sunforge rib far off the shoulder being used by two travelers as shade.
Inside the rig, Brandon rides with one boot braced against the floor, hat low, watching the road rather than Jessie. His satchel is at his feet.
Jessie drives one-handed, goggles pushed up, glancing at a heat shimmer ahead where low buildings begin to resolve.
Small final panel: a hand-painted board appears through the glare: LAST DROP — WATER / SHADE / ROOMS.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not because anybody ran him out of anywhere. He just tends to keep moving.

directionInline.text: Establish the narrator immediately as dry, factual and slightly amused. It may know ordinary facts about people but does not know or explain the larger mystery. Do not make the opening ominous.

title: One Drink
summary: Jessie drops Brandon at the Last Drop for water and food. Their existing arrangement is casual enough that neither calls it companionship yet, but Jessie expects him back at the rig.

panelPlan.text: The rig rolls into the Last Drop settlement: patched roofs, hitching rails, shaded tables, people doing ordinary midday work. The saloon is the darkest doorway in town.
Jessie brakes beside a water trough. Brandon lifts his satchel, then leaves it on the floor after a glance at the saloon.
Brandon steps down into the glare. Jessie leans across the empty seat and nudges his satchel farther from the door with two fingers.
Brandon notices what she did. Jessie has already turned forward again.
Brandon heads toward the saloon. Jessie calls after him from the rig before steering toward shade behind a low outbuilding.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: JESSIE PETRESCU gave him a ride yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither of them has discussed whether that arrangement is still in effect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'll try not to offend it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Because then you'll come back for it.

directionInline.text: Their chemistry should already have mild friction and familiarity, but not intimacy. Jessie is practical, not possessive; Brandon is amused enough not to argue about the bag.

title: Nothing Ever Happens Here
summary: Meet Eva as a bored sixteen-year-old embedded in the Last Drop's ordinary social life. She notices the scarred patron react when Jessie calls Brandon's name from outside, before Brandon himself has done anything interesting.

panelPlan.text: Inside the Last Drop before Brandon enters: dim room, patched bar, flies at the window, lunch plates, card game, boots on chairs. Eva wipes the same stretch of bar for the third time while the bartender counts coins nearby.
Eva watches a traveler outside through the doorway, then looks back at the card game with disappointment.
At a side table, the scarred patron pauses with his cup halfway up. Through the open doorway, Jessie's voice carries in from the street: 'Brandon.'
Brandon's silhouette crosses the threshold a moment later. The patron looks from the doorway toward his face, as if a half-heard name has just found the wrong person.
Eva catches the change in him before she fully looks at Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: She has spent most of the summer waiting for something to happen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: If I wipe this spot again, I think it becomes a religious practice.

directionInline.text: Eva belongs to the place before she leaves it. Give the Last Drop ordinary rhythms and familiar faces. The patron's reaction begins with a plausible mishearing, not a planted message or supernatural recognition.

title: Brannock
summary: The scarred patron has heard Jessie say 'Brandon' through the noise and taken it for 'Brannock.' Brandon resembles the local Brannock closely enough that the mistake hardens into certainty before anyone can correct it.

panelPlan.text: Large panel: Brandon just inside the doorway, still squinting from the glare. The patron stands from his table in the foreground, trying to reconcile the face with the name he thinks he heard.
Close on the patron. He says the name with recognition and old anger, not uncertainty.
Brandon looks over one shoulder toward the door, genuinely checking whether someone else entered behind him.
Eva stops wiping the bar. Several locals glance between the two men.
The patron's hand closes around his bottle. Brandon raises one empty hand, more confused than defensive.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The man at the wall heard BRANNOCK.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Depending on who tells it around the Last Drop, Brannock was a thief, a killer, a hero, or all three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm sorry. You've got the wrong man.

directionInline.text: The first false identity is genuinely accidental. The near-name plus a rough resemblance and an existing local legend are enough for confirmation bias to take over. This is not one of Raina or Samuel's setups.

title: A Bottle
summary: The patron throws a bottle and then himself. Brandon reacts efficiently without turning the room into a showdown; Eva's curiosity becomes personal because Brandon refuses to behave like the returning outlaw everyone expects.

panelPlan.text: The bottle leaves the patron's hand. Brandon tilts aside; glass breaks against the doorframe behind him.
Two nearby patrons shift chairs back. One hand drifts toward a holster, but nobody draws.
The scarred patron lunges. Brandon catches his wrist and shoulder instead of striking him.
Brandon turns with the momentum and folds the man chest-down across an empty table. Cups jump but do not spill.
Eva has moved closer without realizing it, rag still in one hand.
Brandon releases the patron immediately and takes one step back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scarred patron
dialogueInline.text: You think I don't remember you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I think you don't know me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That does seem to be the problem.

directionInline.text: No martial-arts flourish. Brandon's physical competence is practical and proportionate. Eva should be intrigued by the mismatch between the room's expectation and Brandon's behavior.

title: The Darkest Table
summary: Brandon ends the confrontation by sitting down rather than claiming the room. Eva brings him water and invites herself into the empty chair opposite.

panelPlan.text: The patron stays bent over the table catching his breath. Brandon rights the chair the man knocked aside.
Brandon crosses to the darkest table against the wall. The room remains tense because everyone expected a second act.
Brandon sits, removes his gloves and looks toward the bar.
Eva sets a chipped cup of water in front of him. She keeps the second chair pulled out with one foot.
Brandon drinks half the cup before looking at her. She sits anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Could I get some water, please?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Good, because I don't have the explanation.

directionInline.text: Let the room remain active around them. Background locals whisper, resume eating, or keep watching. The story does not freeze into a two-shot just because Eva sits down.

title: Problems He Understands
summary: Eva tries to turn the encounter into a mystery. Brandon is more interested in water and lunch, and accidentally reveals just enough guardedness to make Eva more curious.

panelPlan.text: Eva leans forward over the table while Brandon drinks. A plate of bread, beans and something fried lands between them.
Brandon begins eating. Eva waits exactly one bite before continuing.
Brandon glances toward the scarred patron across the room, who is now whispering to another local.
Eva catches the glance and mistakes it for concern. Brandon notices that she noticed.
His reply about other problems comes out more personal than he intended. He immediately returns his attention to the plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He knew a face. Mine happened to be standing there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I've got enough problems I already understand, I don't much care about ones I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Bah. Leave it alone. I didn't mean anything by that.

directionInline.text: Protect the approved Brandon voice. He is conversational and grammatical, not cryptic. His accidental self-disclosure and retreat should feel like a natural boundary, not a mystery tease.

title: The Story Starts Moving
summary: While Brandon eats, the room begins converting the encounter into a Brannock story in real time. Eva hears contradictions accumulate and realizes Brandon's indifference is not stopping the narrative from growing around him.

panelPlan.text: Across the room, the scarred patron tells two locals something in a low voice. One reacts with disbelief, the other with excitement.
At another table, a different local looks Brandon over and quietly disagrees about some remembered detail.
Eva hears fragments from both conversations while Brandon tears bread into his beans.
The bartender sets a refill down and tells Brandon the back door is available if he wants it.
Brandon looks toward the bright front door, then toward Eva occupying his table like she owns half of it.
At the doorway behind Eva, Jessie appears carrying Brandon's satchel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Brannock had gray in his hair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You are remarkably committed to lunch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It hasn't accused me of anything.

directionInline.text: This page dramatizes social mutation rather than explaining it. Different locals should have different memories and motives. End on Jessie's arrival as the page turn into the travel relationship.

title: Too Hot Here
summary: Jessie has read the town's social temperature from outside and brought Brandon's satchel. Her casual 'we' surprises him more than the warning itself; Eva immediately tries to join the arrangement.

panelPlan.text: Jessie stands just inside the saloon doorway with Brandon's satchel over one shoulder. She surveys the room before addressing him.
Brandon looks at the satchel, then at her. Eva looks between them with new interest.
Jessie nods toward the window, where three locals have begun gathering outside near the rig.
Brandon stands, still holding the last piece of bread.
Eva rises too, as though this has already been decided.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It's too hot here for you. We're leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Fine. I'm leaving. You can come with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I haven't decided whether you're helping.

directionInline.text: Jessie reads people, not prophecy. Her use of 'we' is practical and slightly presumptuous. Eva should clock the relationship instantly and begin inserting herself into it.

title: What Jessie Saw
summary: Outside, Jessie explains the practical reason for leaving: people are beginning to gather around a story rather than an event. Eva interprets Jessie's readiness to leave as evidence that Jessie trusts Brandon more than she admits.

panelPlan.text: The three step into the white glare. Jessie walks straight toward the rig while Brandon adjusts the satchel she handed back.
Across the street, the small knot of locals glance openly at Brandon. One points toward the rear of the saloon.
Eva walks backward in front of Jessie, asking questions while Jessie keeps moving.
Brandon pauses to tie the satchel strap. Eva and Jessie get several steps ahead and continue talking about him as if he is not present.
Brandon looks up at the sound of his own name but does not interrupt yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had his bag before he agreed to go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: There were three men outside deciding whether they remembered him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I believe what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the first real Eva/Jessie relationship scene. The subject is Brandon, but the deeper content is how each woman decides what she believes about a person.

title: Behind the Saloon
summary: The trio is almost out when noise behind the saloon draws Brandon around the corner. The issue turns from social inconvenience to immediate human danger.

panelPlan.text: Jessie reaches the rig and starts checking the front wheel while Eva hovers nearby. Brandon approaches from behind.
A dull wooden knock comes from the back lot, followed by a choking sound too quiet to be a shout.
Brandon stops. Jessie keeps working for one beat, then notices he stopped.
Brandon walks toward the rear corner of the saloon. Eva starts after him. Jessie closes her eyes briefly because she knows they are no longer leaving in ten minutes.
Page-turn panel from Brandon's viewpoint: only a pair of boots visible beyond the corner, kicking several inches above the dirt.

directionInline.text: Use the page turn. Do not reveal the full hanging until Page 12. Jessie's frustration is affectionate only in hindsight; right now it is practical recognition of Brandon's inability to ignore an immediate problem.

title: Dead Weight
summary: Reveal Tomas being publicly hanged in the back lot while Marcus and several locals watch. Brandon does not ask for the history before intervening.

panelPlan.text: Large reveal panel: Tomas hangs from a loading beam behind the saloon, boots scraping empty air. Marcus Kovacs stands with two locals nearby as if supervising unpleasant work.
Brandon takes in the rope, the beam and the barrel beneath it in one glance.
Marcus turns toward him, irritated at the interruption rather than ashamed.
Brandon drags the barrel under Tomas and climbs onto it.
He shoulders Tomas's weight and pulls a knife to the rope.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Behind the Last Drop, Marcus Kovacs is hanging a man named Tomas.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon does not know Tomas either.

directionInline.text: The narrator supplies only facts. Brandon's action should precede any moral speech. He helps because a man is currently choking, not because he has diagnosed the town.

title: Cut the Rope
summary: Brandon cuts Tomas down while Marcus invokes Brannock again. Eva arrives in time to see Brandon prioritize Tomas over the accusation.

panelPlan.text: Brandon saws through the rope while Tomas's weight drives him awkwardly into the barrel.
The rope parts. Brandon and Tomas both fall hard into the dirt.
Brandon rolls Tomas onto his side and works the noose loose from his neck.
Marcus advances holding a short length of pipe. Eva appears at the corner with the water cup she grabbed from inside.
Tomas coughs violently. Brandon looks relieved for exactly one breath.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You always did have to make trouble, Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know Brannock. I know this man is choking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Same righteous act. Same damn timing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Easy, Tomas. Don't try to talk yet.

directionInline.text: Brandon can learn Tomas's name from somebody shouting it during the rescue or from Tomas himself in a rasp; keep that incidental. The important beat is that Brandon's attention remains on the present-tense person.

title: Marcus's Brannock
summary: Marcus tries to force Brandon into Brannock's old role by naming grievances and daring him to deny them. Brandon keeps refusing the premise and tending Tomas, which frustrates Marcus more than a duel would.

panelPlan.text: Marcus plants himself between Brandon and the open yard, pipe loose in one hand. Several locals have gathered at a cautious distance.
Brandon kneels beside Tomas, supporting his shoulders while Eva trickles water over Tomas's lips.
Marcus names an old offense. Brandon does not look up.
Marcus steps closer, forcing Brandon finally to stand between him and Tomas.
Eva sees that the locals are now watching Marcus's behavior rather than simply accepting his version of Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: You burned my brother out of this place.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marcus
dialogueInline.text: Look me in the face and say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm looking at him right now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I know. That's making this harder.

directionInline.text: Marcus should not sound like he is delivering backstory for the reader. Give him personal anger and need for acknowledgment. Brandon's refusal deprives him of the scene he expected.

title: The Wrong Fight
summary: Marcus swings first. Brandon avoids him without escalating into a duel, and the conflict becomes visibly less about Brannock than Marcus's need to maintain control in front of the town.

panelPlan.text: Marcus swings the pipe at Brandon's head. Brandon leans away; the pipe splinters a fence post.
Brandon catches Marcus's forearm on the return swing and redirects him into the wall rather than striking him.
Marcus shoves free, humiliated. A local behind him quietly lowers the hand that had been hovering near a holster.
Tomas coughs from the ground. Eva turns back to him rather than watching the fight.
Brandon steps away from Marcus and kneels again beside Tomas, exposing his back for a moment because he is choosing the injured man over the contest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't have a reason to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Good. Keep him on his side.

directionInline.text: Brandon's dry line should not turn the scene into a quip-fest. His real choice is physical: he returns to Tomas while Marcus still wants the audience.

title: Who Is Watching Whom
summary: Marcus discovers that the crowd's attention has shifted. One local helps Tomas without permission, weakening Marcus's control more than Brandon could have by defeating him.

panelPlan.text: A woman from the watching crowd steps forward with a folded cloth and kneels beside Tomas.
Another local brings a fresh bucket without being told. Marcus sees both acts.
Brandon moves aside enough to let them help. Eva watches the social geometry change.
Marcus raises the pipe again, but nobody moves with him this time.
From beyond the lot comes the rising growl of Jessie's rig.

directionInline.text: This is consequence through community behavior, not a speech. Marcus loses some authority because people act independently while he is focused on the Brannock story.

title: The Rig
summary: Jessie drives into the back lot and turns the possibility of leaving into an immediate choice. Brandon makes sure Tomas is in local hands before moving.

panelPlan.text: Jessie's rig slews into the back lot in a low cloud of dust, stopping close enough to make the open passenger door an argument.
Jessie takes in Tomas, Marcus, Brandon and Eva in one sweep. Her expression says none of this surprises her enough.
Brandon checks Tomas once more with the local woman while Jessie drums two fingers on the wheel.
Marcus moves to block Brandon's path to the rig. The locals do not close ranks behind him.
Brandon stands and hands the cut length of rope to Marcus instead of a weapon.

directionInline.text: Jessie does not rescue Brandon from a fight; she supplies motion. Brandon leaves only after another person has taken responsibility for Tomas.

title: Brandon Mack
summary: Marcus asks the question the whole issue has been circling. Brandon answers with his actual name and leaves Marcus to decide whether to believe it.

panelPlan.text: Marcus blocks the passenger door, pipe lowered but still in hand.
Brandon stops rather than forcing past him. Jessie waits behind the wheel, watching Marcus more than Brandon.
Marcus looks at Brandon with less certainty than before.
Brandon gives his name plainly.
Marcus shifts just enough for Brandon to pass, not conceding belief.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You can keep thinking that. It's still my name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you can tell him about me if he comes back.

directionInline.text: Do not play the last line as a cool-guy mic drop. Brandon is tired of the argument and genuinely means Marcus should save it for the person he wants.

title: The Third Passenger
summary: Brandon climbs into the rig and discovers Eva has already attached herself to the departure. Jessie refuses to stop long enough for Brandon to win the argument.

panelPlan.text: Brandon climbs into the passenger seat. Jessie immediately starts rolling before the door is fully shut.
Brandon looks in the side mirror and sees Eva on the rear step with a small pack.
He twists in his seat. Eva gives him a small wave.
Jessie keeps her eyes on the road as they clear the settlement.
Brandon looks at Jessie. Jessie does not look back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Why is that your answer to everything?

directionInline.text: Eva's departure should feel opportunistic and prepared rather than fated. Jessie's refusal to stop is funny because it is also the practical reason Eva successfully joins them.

title: What He Heard
summary: Once the Last Drop is behind them, Eva reconstructs the first misidentification. Jessie called 'Brandon' from outside; the scarred patron heard 'Brannock' and then made the face fit the story he already knew.

panelPlan.text: Long horizontal: the rig travels across hard white ground. The Last Drop has become a low smudge behind them.
Eva leans between the seats, replaying the moment in her head instead of producing a clue or artifact.
A small memory inset: Jessie at the rig calling 'Brandon' toward the saloon door while the scarred patron turns inside.
Another memory inset: Brandon enters and the patron's uncertain recognition turns certain.
Back in the rig, Brandon accepts the mundane explanation more readily than Eva does.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Jessie called your name before you walked in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He already had a Brannock in his head. Then you walked in looking close enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: People have done worse with less.

directionInline.text: Do not sneak a mystery clue back into this page. Issue 1 works because the first identity can be explained completely as human error plus expectation. The larger pattern begins only when later cases stop fitting that explanation.

title: Careful Answers
summary: Eva and Jessie compare what the Brannock mistake revealed about Brandon and about the Last Drop while he can plainly hear them. Their theories about him become the first real conversation between the two women.

panelPlan.text: Eva leans between the seats from behind, still holding the note. Jessie keeps driving.
Eva points out that Jessie had Brandon's bag ready before he decided to leave.
Jessie answers without taking the bait completely. Brandon stares out the side window, listening.
Eva studies Jessie instead of Brandon for the first time.
Brandon finally interrupts when the conversation becomes openly about whether Jessie trusts him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The speed is the part I don't like.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't agreeing with you. I was narrowing the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You still had his bag ready before any of this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Marcus had a pipe before any of this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I trust what I've seen him do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't know him well enough for a careless one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can still hear both of you.

directionInline.text: This is the deliberate early Brandon-centered Eva/Jessie dialogue architecture. Their disagreement about what counts as evidence reveals how each woman thinks and creates the first intimacy between them.

title: Dust on the Lens
summary: The accidental trio continues into the Sunfields. Brandon remains himself; the Brannock mistake remains behind them but has already acquired a social life of its own, establishing both the group and the series engine without requiring a conspiracy.

panelPlan.text: Wide panel: the rig passes a half-buried black Sunforge shape where two workers have hung a shade cloth from it. Nobody in the rig comments on it.
Inside, Eva folds the note carefully and keeps it. Brandon sees her do it and decides not to ask for it back.
Brandon looks from Eva to Jessie, then out at the empty road ahead.
Jessie asks the practical question nobody has answered yet.

Final wide panel: the rig small against the Sunfields, three figures now traveling together. In a narrow inset at the bottom, back at the Last Drop, two locals are already retelling the hanging to someone who was not there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Do either of you know where we're going?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By sundown, Brandon Mack is still a drifter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Back at the Last Drop, Brannock has already started traveling too.

directionInline.text: End on two simultaneous beginnings: the trio and the independent social life of the false identity. The Sunforge remains ordinary background texture. The narrator may create irony, but should not explain why any of this is happening.
